13.0.s.en: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

13.0.0.en: The mixed multitude: the Gentiles who went with the children of Israel and dwelt among them and did not join the faith of the Jews. Among them were a great number of Moabites and Ammonites, who lived adjoining the people of God.

13.0.1.en: Before beginning his reforms, Nehemiah took care to read the Holy Bible publicly to the people assembled before him in the Temple. By the providence of God, on that day they read in the twenty-third chapter of the book of Deuteronomy, and found written in it that the Law commands keeping away from the Ammonites and Moabites, because they bear enmity to the children of Israel and so draw them to the worship of their gods (Deut 23:3-5). The people responded to the word of God and obeyed the Law, so they separated and put out from among them all the Moabites and Ammonites, and by this they got rid of what caused them to stumble and kept them far from God. The text of the Law here does not intend racial discrimination, but keeping away from evil and from the evil association that causes the children of God to fall and separates them from Him, just as the tribe of Reuben housed the Moabites in its midst, and they led the Jews in the worship of Chemosh their god, and moreover enslaved them under the leadership of Eglon their king for eighteen years. God permitted strangers who join the faith in Him to offer sacrifices to Him (Num 15:14) and received Ruth the Moabitess into His people, so that she married Boaz, and moreover Christ came from her seed.

13.1.0.en: As a result of the negligence of the priests and their marriage to foreign women from the Gentiles, there was a kinship between Eliashib the high priest and Tobiah the Ammonite, who had resisted the building of the wall, and this formed a friendship between them. So when matters had calmed and years had passed after the building of the wall, Tobiah was able by his influence to persuade Eliashib the high priest to set aside for him a large room in the Temple, in which to stay when he visited Jerusalem. This room had been set apart for storing the contributions offered by the people, namely the incense and the vessels of the Temple, and also the people's tithes of wheat, wine and oil, which were distributed to the Levites and the priests. So Eliashib emptied the room and prepared it as a dwelling for Tobiah his relative, although the Law forbids the entrance of the Gentiles into the Temple, and especially the Ammonites (v. 1; Deut 23:3). How then could Tobiah enter and dwell there?

13.1.1.en: Thus we see Eliashib's great negligence in two matters:

13.1.2.en: 1- Bringing Tobiah into the Temple to dwell beside it, as a result of the kinship between them, defying God and His Law.

13.1.3.en: 2- His neglect of the needs of the Levites and the equipment of the Temple, for he took out everything that was in the storehouses, which exposed it to spoiling.

13.1.4.en: Perhaps his preparing “the great chamber” for Tobiah was done by buying splendid furniture, or by joining several rooms together to be a dwelling worthy of Tobiah his relative.

13.2.0.en: This great error into which Eliashib fell happened during the absence of Nehemiah with King Artaxerxes. Eliashib seized the opportunity of Nehemiah's not being in Jerusalem, and honored Tobiah at the expense of the house of God. Perhaps intermarriage had taken place between the seed of Eliashib and the seed of Tobiah in this period, and visits, exchange of gifts and honors took place between them, among them this honor of preparing a chamber for Tobiah in the Temple. This shows the importance of the presence of the spiritual leader, for Nehemiah represented the truth and the voice of God, and the people and the priests feared him, although it should have been Eliashib the high priest who was the spiritual leader, who proclaims the fear of God and the necessity of holding fast to His Law. This reminds us of the sin of Aaron when he made the golden calf in the period of Moses' absence on the mountain to receive God's commandments and Law (Ex 32:4). As for Nehemiah's return to the king in the thirty-second year of the reign of Artaxerxes, that is, after twelve years he had spent in Jerusalem, it was either because of an appointed time agreed upon with the king at which he would return to Babylon, or because the king summoned Nehemiah to be reassured about the condition of Jerusalem and Judea, over which Nehemiah was governor on behalf of the king.

13.2.1.en: Hold fast to the truth and the commandments of God, even if those around you draw away from them. By this you protect yourself from the wars of the devil, enjoy the care of God and are a light to the world. And God gives you awe in the eyes of others, even if they pretend to resist you or mock you, for the power of God that is in you will affect their hearts.

13.3.0.en: Nehemiah was greatly distressed when he saw the defilement of the Temple by the dwelling of Tobiah the pagan inside it, and the negligence of Eliashib, who should have been the first to defend the Temple and be careful for its purity. So he came forward with courage, not fearing the influence of Tobiah nor the authority of Eliashib the high priest, and took out all Tobiah's belongings and threw them outside the Temple. Then he commanded, and the priests purified the chamber in which Tobiah had dwelt, as the Law requires. After that he brought back into the chamber the vessels of the house of the Lord, the incense and all the gifts that the people had offered to the Temple to be a portion for the Levites.

13.3.2.en: 1- When Eliashib was negligent, Nehemiah came forward and did what Eliashib should have done. He did not keep silent, although he was the governor and not the high priest, but took care to carry out the Law, since the high priest had been negligent.

13.3.3.en: 2- Nehemiah did not take Tobiah's belongings for himself, but wished to be rid of them by throwing them outside the Temple, so that Eliashib or Tobiah might take them, but that they might not defile the Temple of God. In this he resembles Christ, who drove the sellers out of the Temple, them and all their belongings, that the house of God might remain a house of prayer (Mt 21:13).

13.3.4.en: 3- Nehemiah's care for the needs of the priests and Levites, so that they would not be hindered from their service of the Temple.

13.3.5.en: 4- His honoring of the vessels of the house of the Lord and its needs of incense and the like.

13.3.6.en: If a person falls into sin, he must be rid of all its sources and purify himself by repentance and confession, so that he can approach to partake of the Holy Mysteries and his heart becomes a dwelling for God alone; as Nehemiah got rid of Tobiah's belongings and purified the chamber, and then brought the vessels of the house of the Lord and the gifts of the people into the chamber.

13.3.8.en: 10- And I perceived that the portions of the Levites had not been given them: for the Levites and the singers, that did the work, were fled every one to his field. 11- Then contended I with the rulers, and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them together, and set them in their place.

13.3.9.en: 12- Then brought all Judah the tithe of the corn and the new wine and the oil unto the treasuries. 13- And I made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah: and next to them was Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah: for they were counted faithful, and their office was to distribute unto their brethren. 14- Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for the offices thereof.

13.4.0.en: When Nehemiah entered the Temple to purify it of Tobiah's belongings, he noticed the absence of the Levites from the Temple; he did not hear the praise of the singers, and he learned that the people no longer offered their tithes and gifts in the Temple. The reason may have been that the people knew that their gifts had been thrown out of the Temple to prepare a chamber for Tobiah, or that Tobiah had also seized them, so they no longer offered their offerings. As a result the Levites did not find what they needed and were compelled to go to the fields to work in them so as to find their food, and they left the service of the house of the Lord. What is strange is that none of this concerned Eliashib the high priest, because of his being absorbed in honoring Tobiah, nor did it concern the rulers, that is, the leaders of the people, who were occupied with their positions; perhaps they fell into the sin of seizing part of the portions of the Levites, and the gifts were divided between the priests and the rulers. In short, the Levites did not find their food, so they looked for other work to meet their needs.

13.5.0.en: The first reform that Nehemiah carried out was that he stood as an adversary to the rulers and rebuked them because they had not stood against Eliashib and had left the gifts of the Temple to be thrown outside the storehouses, so that the people doubted whether their gifts reached the Levites, and they did not encourage the people to return to paying the tithes. His second reform was that he sent and called Levites from every place in Judea and gathered them to the Temple, and set each one of them in his service according to the arrangement that had been in force before he traveled to the king, and by this the service returned to the Temple as it had been.

13.5.1.en: It is noticed that he did not rebuke the Levites, because they were excusable, for they were compelled to look for their food by working in the fields. It was not their intention to leave the service of the Temple, but the error of Eliashib and the error of the people toward them, as we mentioned, drove them to leave the Temple. Nehemiah was positive: although he did not blame them for leaving the service, he brought them back to their service, and so they gave up their attachment to the fields and material gain; that is, he restored them to devote themselves to the service of God.

13.6.0.en: The rulers, the assistants of Nehemiah, that is, the leaders of the people, moved and called the people to offer the tithes and contributions to the Temple, as they had formerly pledged (ch. 10:39). They were encouraged when they saw the zeal of Nehemiah, faithful for the house of the Lord, and they offered their gifts of wheat, wine and oil.

13.7.0.en: To organize the collection of the people's gifts and their distribution to the priests and Levites, Nehemiah appointed a group of priests and Levites known for faithfulness, accuracy and bearing responsibility, and gave them the responsibility of the storehouses in the Temple. This is the third reform that Nehemiah carried out, and it shows his excellence in administration and the organization of works.

13.8.0.en: In all that he did, Nehemiah did not look for a reward from anyone, but did everything for God's sake. He is a man of prayer, and he ended what he did in the preceding verses with a prayer in which he asked God to remember him with mercy for the forgiveness of his sins, and he besought God not to forget any good deed he had done by the power of God in Jerusalem, such as the building of the wall.

13.8.1.en: What has gone before and what comes in this chapter show the importance of the leader in leading others to obey God and His commandments. In Nehemiah's presence great achievements were made, which we saw in the first twelve chapters of this book, but when he was absent for a little while with the king, the people returned to their sins and negligence. Yet by the grace of God and the faithfulness of Nehemiah they returned again to God, as appears from this chapter.

13.8.2.en: Be careful to hold fast to the commandments of God and to fulfill your responsibilities, because you are responsible for those around you: your drawing near to God brings them near to Him, and your drawing away from Him makes them stumble and draws them away from Him.

13.8.4.en: 15- In those days saw I in Judah some treading wine presses on the sabbath, and bringing in sheaves, and lading asses; as also wine, grapes, and figs, and all manner of burdens, which they brought into Jerusalem on the sabbath day: and I testified against them in the day wherein they sold victuals. 16- There dwelt men of Tyre also therein, which brought fish, and all manner of ware, and sold on the sabbath unto the children of Judah, and in Jerusalem. 17- Then I contended with the nobles of Judah, and said unto them, What evil thing is this that ye do, and profane the sabbath day? 18- Did not your fathers thus, and did not our God bring all this evil upon us, and upon this city? yet ye bring more wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath. 19- And it came to pass, that when the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the sabbath, I commanded that the gates should be shut, and charged that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and some of my servants set I at the gates, that there should no burden be brought in on the sabbath day. 20- So the merchants and sellers of all kind of ware lodged without Jerusalem once or twice. 21- Then I testified against them, and said unto them, Why lodge ye about the wall? if ye do so again, I will lay hands on you. From that time forth came they no more on the sabbath. 22- And I commanded the Levites that they should cleanse themselves, and that they should come and keep the gates, to sanctify the sabbath day. Remember me, O my God, concerning this also, and spare me according to the greatness of thy mercy.

13.9.0.en: Nehemiah also noticed, as he went about in Jerusalem, that some of the Jews were treading grapes in the wine presses to press them, and this was on the Sabbath day, on which it is forbidden to do any material work, so that the Jews might devote themselves to the worship of God.

13.9.1.en: He also saw in the fields the farmers gathering the sheaves of their harvest and binding them, and the porters loading the donkeys with burdens to carry from place to place, and all these works were forbidden on the Sabbath day (Ex 34:21; Deut 5:14; Jer 17:21). The Jews do not work, and likewise they let their animals rest on the Sabbath day.

13.9.2.en: He also found on the Sabbath day Jews coming from the various lands to Jerusalem with wares of wine, grapes and figs to sell on that day, and of course trade was forbidden on the Sabbath day. Here appears the exactness of Nehemiah, who went about himself to care for his people and correct their errors, especially after he found the deviation of the priests under Eliashib and the slackness of the rulers. So he relied on himself in examining everything, until matters were put right, and after this each one would do his own work.

13.9.3.en: He declares clearly that he testified against them, that is, he made known to them their sin in breaking the Sabbath. He did not punish them, but taught them the Law and called them to follow it. In this he had no personal anger against them, but firmness in carrying out the commandment of God, which is the fourth of the Ten Commandments, which requires keeping the Sabbath (Ex 20:8).

13.10.0.en: Tyre was a coastal city on the Mediterranean Sea, and was the most famous city in the world in trade. Near it lay Sidon, famous for fishing, and they used to bring this fish to sell in Jerusalem. Because of the considerable distance between Tyre and Jerusalem, they most likely salted the fish so that it could endure the journey. These Tyrians had temporary dwellings in Jerusalem, but their permanent places of residence were in Tyre.

13.10.1.en: Because the Jews broke the Sabbath and sold and bought on it, this encouraged the Tyrians, that is, the Gentiles, to come to sell this fish and all their wares in Jerusalem and the surrounding cities.

13.11.0.en: Nehemiah stood as an adversary to the elders and leaders of the people, and rebuked them for breaking the fourth commandment of God, which is the sanctification of the Sabbath day for His worship; in this they profane the Sabbath day and anger God. Nehemiah here is a type of Christ the Judge, who will call all to account for their sins; for the sin of the leaders was not only that they sold and bought on the Sabbath, but that they allowed the people to do so, and so they made them stumble by this negligence. Their conduct may have led to negligence about the Sabbath by doing works other than trade.

13.12.0.en: Nehemiah added, and reminded the leaders that negligence in breaking the Sabbath and the other commandments of God is what brought the Babylonian captivity upon Jerusalem and Judea, after the kingdom of Israel had been taken captive. Because the people in ancient times neglected the rest of the seventh year and sowed the land against the commandment of God, the land enjoyed her sabbaths, that is, the land rested from cultivation for seventy years, the period of the Babylonian captivity, in place of the Jews' neglect of the commandment of the seventh year for 490 years (2 Chr 36:21). And Nehemiah said to the leaders before the people that by this they were increasing the wrath of God against His city Jerusalem. So the leaders and all the people wept because of their breaking of the Sabbath, and became ready to carry out the commandment.

13.13.0.en: Nehemiah took definite decisions concerning the keeping of the Sabbath, which were:

13.13.1.en: 1- He testified, with his assistants, against the merchants who sold and bought on the Sabbath day (v. 15).

13.13.2.en: 2- He rebuked the leaders, who represent all the people, for their breaking of the Sabbath day, and so exposing themselves to the divine wrath (vv. 17, 18).

13.13.3.en: 3- At the end of Friday, when darkness covered the gates of Jerusalem, announcing the beginning of the night of the Sabbath, Nehemiah commanded that the gates be shut and not be opened until the whole Sabbath day had ended.

13.13.4.en: Then Nehemiah appointed some of his assistants as watchers over all the gates of Jerusalem, to make sure that the commandment to keep the Sabbath was carried out.

13.14.0.en: Although Nehemiah's orders were definite and strong, the merchants thought that it was merely a temporary severity on his part, which he would forget and be distracted from in time. So they came with their wares on the next Sabbath, but the gates of Jerusalem remained shut and no one entered. When this was repeated on the following Sabbath and Nehemiah learned of it, he testified against them concerning this sin, which was their intention to break the Sabbath.

13.14.1.en: Nehemiah was not content with this, but threatened them that if they came on the next Sabbath with wares and lodged outside the city at the gates, he would seize them and throw them into prison for attempting to break the Sabbath. Here we find Nehemiah's firmness in carrying out the commandment and his watching of the gates to prevent the breaking of the Sabbath, and even his threatening those who tried to break the commandment, so that he was able to end this evil within two weeks.

13.14.2.en: Be strict against sin and stop its sources, while examining yourself every day and committing yourself to the sacrament of confession, and you will be able to be rid of it by the power of God.

13.15.0.en: To keep the gates of Jerusalem shut continually on the Sabbath, Nehemiah appointed officials from the Levites over every gate, to guarantee that the commandment was carried out, and by this the people kept the Sabbath and devoted themselves in it to the worship of God.

13.15.1.en: Holding fast to this commandment continued from the days of Nehemiah, that is, in the fifth century before the birth of Christ, until the days of Christ, to the point that the scribes and Pharisees held literally to keeping the Sabbath with all exactness, so that they resisted Christ when they thought He had broken the Sabbath, although He did not break it in any material matters, but did good on the Sabbath, which is the healing of the sick.

13.15.2.en: Nehemiah ends his work in keeping the Sabbath with a prayer in which he asks God to bless him and have mercy on him and bless his holding fast to the commandment. This confirms that Nehemiah is a man of prayer and humble, who asks the compassion and mercies of God. He does not boast of doing good, but feels that he is a sinner in need of God's mercy.

13.15.3.en: Nehemiah asked the Levites to purify themselves, that is, to wash and wash their clothes and keep away from any uncleanness, before their guarding of the gates of Jerusalem, considering this guarding a holy work because it is the carrying out of the fourth commandment. So he made them feel the importance of guarding the gates, especially since he was about to return to the king after a while, and so would have placed this guard in faithful hands, namely the Levites, that they might keep the commandment out of their love for God.

13.15.5.en: 23- In those days also saw I Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab:

13.15.6.en: 24- And their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews' language, but according to the language of each people. 25- And I contended with them, and cursed them, and smote certain of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God, saying, Ye shall not give your daughters unto their sons, nor take their daughters unto your sons, or for yourselves.

13.15.7.en: 26- Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? yet among many nations was there no king like him, who was beloved of his God, and God made him king over all Israel: nevertheless even him did outlandish women cause to sin. 27- Shall we then hearken unto you to do all this great evil, to transgress against our God in marrying strange wives? 28- And one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite: therefore I chased him from me.

13.15.8.en: 29- Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood, and the covenant of the priesthood, and of the Levites. 30- Thus cleansed I them from all strangers, and appointed the wards of the priests and the Levites, every one in his business; 31- And for the wood offering, at times appointed, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, O my God, for good.

13.16.0.en: In negligence the people of God disobeyed their Law and married idolatrous women from the lands surrounding them. One was Ashdod, which is one of the five great cities of the Philistines, lying on the Mediterranean Sea, that is, west of the dwelling of the people of God and beside it, adjoining it. They also married from Moab and the children of Ammon, two peoples who dwell east of the land of the Jews and adjoining it.

13.16.1.en: These marriages led to the begetting of children who could not speak well the language of the people of God, which is the Hebrew language, which they had kept throughout the period of the captivity. The language of Ashdod is close in pronunciation to Hebrew but differs from it, and Nehemiah was greatly distressed when he noticed this strange speech spread among the people of God.

13.16.2.en: It is noted that Ezra, some years earlier, had played a great part in keeping away from the foreign wives (Ezra 9, 10), but they were negligent and went back to these marriages. So the importance of Nehemiah's following up the carrying out of the Law appeared, in this matter in particular, which sadly leads to the worship of idols, since the people worship the idolatrous gods in honor of their wives.

13.17.0.en: Nehemiah saw the people's absorption in marrying idolatrous women and their attachment to them to the point that separation was difficult, so he carried out the Law as it is (Deut 7:3) and did these things with them in order to separate them from the foreign women:

13.17.1.en: 1- He contended with them, that is, he stood as an adversary to them, declaring the Law of God which condemns them.

13.17.2.en: 2- He cursed them, that is, he declared to them the divine curses which they deserved for breaking the Law.

13.17.3.en: 3- He smote them as the Law prescribed (Deut 25:2, 3), and of course this smiting was done through his assistants.

13.17.4.en: 4- He plucked off their hair, and this was not only discipline but contempt for them, because the hair of the beard represents the awe and respect due to elders.

13.17.5.en: 5- He made them swear, that is, he made them take an oath to separate from marriage with the foreign women, and not to marry any foreign women afterward, or allow their children to enter these sinful marriages.

13.17.6.en: And this making them swear is what the Law prescribed (Deut 7:3). By this he placed these men who had transgressed the Law face to face with God, so that they would afterward fear breaking the Law, and if they broke it they would deserve punishment.

13.18.0.en: Nehemiah showed the people the seriousness of marriage with foreign women: not only that it is against the Law of God (v. 25), but he also gave a practical example of the hideousness of this sin, which is what happened with King Solomon, who was beloved of God, but this sin brought the wrath of God upon him. Adversaries to him appeared in his kingdom who rebelled against him, although he was king over all Israel, and the kingdom was divided after him, because he pleased his idolatrous wives and made images of strange gods in Jerusalem, which greatly provoked God. Thus he lost his greatness in wisdom and wealth because of his attachment to idolatrous women. Therefore every person is exposed to ruin if he is attached to idolatry, because he is no better than Solomon, who was very wise.

13.19.0.en: Because of all that preceded concerning the seriousness of the sin of attachment to idolaters, Nehemiah declared that he would not keep silent about this existing evil, that is, the strange marriages that were before him at that time. Nehemiah had persuaded the people of the decision he would take, which was separation from the idolatrous women, before he took the decision. Thus Nehemiah's ability in managing the affairs of the kingdom appears, even in the hardest matters, which were the existing marriages that had produced forbidden children, because he persuaded the people that it was a great treachery against God.

13.20.0.en: Nehemiah's courage appeared when he found one of the grandsons of the high priest Eliashib married to an idolatrous woman, the daughter of Sanballat the Horonite, who had resisted Nehemiah in the building of the wall. He rebuked him and asked him to separate from his wife and return to God, but he refused, so Nehemiah was compelled to drive him out of the priesthood and from membership in the people of God. Sanballat received him with welcome, as Josephus the historian mentions, and built him a temple in which to serve idolatrous gods on Mount Gerizim, and the name of this priest was Manasseh. Perhaps this mountain is what is meant in the words of the Samaritan woman with Christ (Jn 4:20).

13.21.0.en: Nehemiah was in great anger because of the defilement of this place, and perhaps there were with him other priests and Levites who had also entered idolatrous marriages. It was expected of the priests and Levites that they would be an example to the people in holding fast to the Law. Therefore Nehemiah asked God to remember them, to warn them to repent of their evil and separate from marriages with idolatrous women, or to allow them afflictions, perhaps so that they might feel the hideousness of their sins and repent. It also means Nehemiah's appeal to the justice of God, who punishes those who persist in breaking His Law.

13.22.0.en: Nehemiah purified the whole people from every strange marriage by separating from these wives and keeping away from them, and whoever persisted in his attachment to his wife he drove out and set apart from the people of God. After the driving out of those who persisted in evil, the service was not shaken, for Nehemiah redistributed the priests and Levites to their various services to fill the place of those who persisted in the idolatrous marriage and kept away from the service. So he organized the service of guarding, the offering of wood and the collecting of the firstfruits, each offering at its time, and likewise all the works of service inside the Temple.

13.22.1.en: In the end Nehemiah, the man of prayer, lifts up his heart to God, seeking from Him blessing and good, for he does all this for Him alone and asks nothing for himself, because his good comes to him from God.

13.22.2.en: Beware of being attached to any person who draws you away from God, whatever the motives, for the salvation of your soul is more important than anything in the world. And if you have become attached, ask the help of God, that you may courageously be rid of what hinders your spiritual growth.

13.22.3.en: A summary of the most important personalities in the life of Nehemiah

13.22.4.en: 1- Nehemiah is a Hebrew word meaning “Yahweh has shown compassion.”

13.22.5.en: 2- He was born in the captivity, and God gave him a high position with King Artaxerxes, namely the king's cupbearer.

13.22.6.en: 3- He loved God, and his position in the Persian state did not distract him from his worship of God, his prayers and his fasts.

13.22.7.en: 4- His heart was attached to the holy city Jerusalem and the house of the Lord that is in it, so he inquired of his brethren the Jews who had visited Jerusalem about its news, and when he learned that its walls were broken down and its gates burned, he was deeply moved, wept and prayed much to God.

13.22.8.en: 5- Nehemiah the son of Hachaliah was not a priest like Ezra, or a prophet like Haggai, or of the royal seed like Zerubbabel; he was an ordinary Jewish person who obtained a great position in the state, but his heart was attached to God and he felt his responsibility toward the holy city Jerusalem.

13.22.9.en: 6- He was distinguished by courage, for he did not hide his sorrow when he stood to perform his office before the king, although this exposed him to great danger; but because he prayed, God gave him favor in the eyes of the king, who asked him the reason for his sorrow, and when he learned it he sympathized with him and heard his requests and fulfilled them all for him, for the care of Jerusalem (ch. 1).

13.22.10.en: 7- He led the third company returning from the captivity to Jerusalem, and that was in the year 445 BC, thirteen years after the return of Ezra. Its number was small and the exact number is not mentioned, and he had with him a permit from the king to obtain timber for the gates of Jerusalem from the king's forests (ch. 2:8).

13.22.11.en: 8- He inspected the wall of Jerusalem as soon as he arrived, organized the work of building the wall among the clans of the Jews, and encouraged the people with great zeal, so that he was able to build the wall in 52 days (ch. 6:15), and he dedicated the wall in a great celebration (ch. 12).

13.22.12.en: 9- He faced violent resistance from the enemies of the Jews who dwelt around him, but he was strong and continued the work with courage, and God revealed their tricks to him, so they did not hinder him from completing the wall (ch. 3, 4, 6).

13.22.13.en: 10- He remained governor over Jerusalem and Judea for twelve years, after which he returned to Shushan, the palace, the capital of the Persian state, and then returned a second time to complete his rule and his care for his people (ch. 5:14).

13.22.14.en: 11- He relied on prayer together with work in building the wall and preparing for war by bearing arms to defend Jerusalem before the enemies; that is, prayer was joined with striving and work (ch. 3, 4, 6), and he offered a fervent prayer for himself and his people (ch. 9).

13.22.15.en: 12- He took care to solve the internal problems of the people, that is, sympathy for the poor and for those enslaved by their fellow Jews (ch. 5:1-6).

13.22.16.en: 13- He was distinguished by giving and generosity and by not exploiting the poor people to take from them the money assigned to the governor; rather he spent from the funds of his position in the Persian state, and made tables for those gathered with him in the governor's palace (ch. 5:14-19).

13.22.17.en: 14- After the building of the wall Nehemiah took care to organize the guarding of the city of Jerusalem (ch. 7).

13.22.18.en: 15- He took care to establish the genealogies of those returning from the captivity and to repopulate the city of Jerusalem with inhabitants from the returnees (ch. 7).

13.22.19.en: 16- Nehemiah was a wise manager, as appeared in his talk with the king, for he presented his requests in a definite form; and when he reached Jerusalem he inspected the wall, made a plan for the building, organized the building companies and the places of repair, followed the work himself, and faced the resistance of the enemies with divine wisdom, so that he was not hindered from his work.

13.22.20.en: 17- He took care of the spiritual life of his people, and Ezra the priest shared this with him, so he read to them the book of the Law and organized the celebration of the Feast of Tabernacles (ch. 8).

13.22.21.en: 18- After his return from Shushan (the capital of the Persian state) to Jerusalem, Nehemiah took care of the internal reforms: he took care of collecting the tithes and establishing the Levites in their service, purified the Temple of the vessels and belongings of Tobiah the Ammonite, the enemy of the people of God, sanctified the Sabbath day and prevented trade in it (ch. 13).

13.22.22.en: 19- He was firm with those who had married idolatrous women, so he rebuked them and punished them, because they had returned to this sin after Ezra had warned them more than thirteen years earlier (ch. 13).

13.22.23.en: 20- He was a contemporary of the prophet Malachi, the last of the prophets of the Old Testament, who prophesied around the year 433 BC.

13.22.24.en: 21- Nehemiah remained governor of Jerusalem for twelve years, during which he built the wall and carried out his spiritual reforms, then returned to Shushan, the palace, for a short time, and came back to Jerusalem to correct the spiritual errors into which they had fallen in the period of his absence, and remained governor over Jerusalem, caring for it civilly and spiritually. Types of Christ and the Church. Nehemiah is a type of Christ

13.22.26.en: Nehemiah took care to build the wall of Jerusalem and its broken-down gates (ch. 6:15), and Christ rebuilt our nature by His redemption and made us living stones in His Church.

13.22.28.en: Nehemiah was distinguished by contentment, so he gave up what was collected from the people for the governor and spent from his own funds for the needy (ch. 5:14, 16), and Christ was born in a manger and lived poor and took care to feed the crowds by blessing the two fish and the five loaves and the seven loaves and the few small fish.

13.22.30.en: It is mentioned of Nehemiah in his book that he prayed ten times, and Christ would withdraw and spend the whole night in prayer.

13.22.32.en: Nehemiah divided the Jews into groups in the building of the wall (ch. 3), and Christ made the crowds sit down by fifties and by hundreds when He fed them with the fish and the bread.

13.22.34.en: Nehemiah threw Tobiah's belongings outside the Temple, shut the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath, threatened the merchants who lodged outside the city on the Sabbath, and drove the priests who had made strange marriages away from service in the Temple (ch. 13), and Christ drove the sellers out of the Temple and pronounced the woes upon the scribes and Pharisees.

13.22.36.en: Nehemiah gave up his position in the king's palace and went to labor in Jerusalem to build the wall. And Christ left His heavenly glory, became incarnate and redeemed us on the Cross.

13.22.38.en: Nehemiah mourned when he heard of the broken-down walls of Jerusalem and the burned gates (ch. 1), and Christ wept over Jerusalem, which was spiritually broken down because it refused repentance.

13.22.40.en: Nehemiah endured the resistance of the wicked until he completed the building of the wall (ch. 3-6), and Christ endured the temptation on the mountain and all the resistance of the scribes, the Pharisees and the priests.
